title: EIP-7594: PeerDAS - Peer Data Availability Sampling
description: Introducing simple DAS utilizing gossip distribution and peer requests. Extends EIP-4844 blobs using 1D erasure coding, column-based sampling, and introduces a 6-blob-per-transaction limit.

sub_graphs.name: 1D Erasure Coding Extension
sub_graphs.description: Extends EIP-4844 blobs using one-dimensional Reed-Solomon erasure coding. Each blob (row) is extended into CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB cells, doubling the original data via erasure coding. Cells are the smallest authenticated units. The extended data forms a matrix with MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK rows and NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS (128) columns.

invariants.text: FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB == 2 * FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB: the extended blob always has exactly twice the field elements of the original blob.
CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB == FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB // FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL: the number of cells per extended blob is derived deterministically from field element counts.
NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS == CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB (= 128): the number of columns in the data matrix equals the number of cells per extended blob.
Each cell can be independently verified against its blob's KZG commitment using its cell KZG proof.

pre_conditions.text: Input blob must satisfy len(blob) == BYTES_PER_BLOB.

post_conditions.text: compute_cells returns exactly CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB cells for each input blob.
compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs returns both CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB cells and CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB KZG proofs.

Converts trusted CosetEvals back into an untrusted Cell by serializing field elements.

sub_graphs.name: KZG Polynomial Commitment Verification
sub_graphs.description: Defines the KZG-based cryptographic verification mechanism for cells. Implements a universal verification equation for batch-verifying that cells belong to their corresponding commitments using pairings over BLS12-381.

invariants.text: verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch returns True if and only if all cells are valid evaluations of their respective committed polynomials at the specified coset indices.
The batch verification challenge r is deterministically derived via Fiat-Shamir heuristic from all prover-provided data, ensuring non-interactivity.
Commitments in the batch verification must contain no duplicates: len(commitments) == len(set(commitments)).

post_conditions.text: Returns bool indicating whether all provided cells pass the pairing-based verification equation.

Lagrange interpolation produces the lowest-degree polynomial passing through all given points.

sub_graphs.name: Data Reconstruction
sub_graphs.description: Implements Reed-Solomon erasure code recovery. Given at least 50% of all columns (cells) for a blob, the original polynomial and all cells/proofs can be recovered using FFT-based techniques. This is the key availability guarantee of PeerDAS.

invariants.text: Reconstruction requires at least CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB / 2 cells (50% of columns). This is the fundamental recovery threshold of the erasure code.
No duplicate cell indices are allowed in the input: len(cell_indices) == len(set(cell_indices)).
The recovered polynomial has degree at most FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB - 1, matching the original blob polynomial.

post_conditions.text: Returns the complete set of CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB cells and CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB KZG proofs for the blob.
The recovered polynomial_coeff has exactly FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB coefficients (truncated from extended domain).

functions.description: Given at least 50% of cells for a blob, recovers all cells and proofs using FFT-based Reed-Solomon recovery. Public method.
Recovers the original polynomial in coefficient form from partial cell evaluations using vanishing polynomial division over a coset FFT domain.
Computes the polynomial that vanishes at every point corresponding to missing cells. Used in erasure code recovery.
Recovers the full matrix of cells and proofs for all blobs given a partial matrix with at least 50% columns per blob.

sub_graphs.name: Data Matrix and Column Sidecar Construction
sub_graphs.description: Defines the data matrix structure (rows = blobs, columns = cell indices) and the construction of DataColumnSidecar objects for distribution. Each column sidecar packages the cells from a specific column index across all blobs in a block, along with KZG commitments, proofs, and a signed block header.

invariants.text: The matrix has exactly NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS (128) columns and up to MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK_FULU (12) rows.
Each DataColumnSidecar contains cells from exactly one column index across all blobs in the block.
len(cells_and_kzg_proofs) == len(blob_kzg_commitments): each blob has corresponding cells and proofs.

sub_graphs.name: Custody Groups and Node Assignment
sub_graphs.description: Defines the deterministic, public custody assignment mechanism. Columns are grouped into custody groups and nodes are assigned custody groups as a pseudorandom function of their node ID.

invariants.text: custody_group_count <= NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS (128): a node cannot custody more groups than exist.
Custody selection is deterministic and public: any party can compute a node's custody groups from its node_id and custody_group_count.
Increasing custody_size extends the returned custody list (not a complete reshuffle), ensuring backward compatibility.
Returned custody groups contain no duplicates: len(custody_groups) == len(set(custody_groups)).
Nodes MUST custody all columns in each of their assigned custody groups.
Validator custody requirement is min(max(total_node_balance // BALANCE_PER_ADDITIONAL_CUSTODY_GROUP, VALIDATOR_CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT), NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS).

post_conditions.text: get_custody_groups returns exactly custody_group_count unique, sorted custody group indices.
compute_columns_for_custody_group returns columns_per_group sorted column indices.

sub_graphs.name: Custody Sampling Protocol
sub_graphs.description: Defines the per-slot data availability sampling procedure. Each node downloads a minimum number of columns per slot, determined by max(SAMPLES_PER_SLOT, custody_group_count * columns_per_group).

invariants.text: sampling_size = max(SAMPLES_PER_SLOT, custody_group_count * columns_per_group): the sampling set always includes the custody set.
Sampling is successful if and only if the node retrieves ALL selected columns for the slot.
The sampling column set is a superset of the custody column set, ensuring consistency.

pre_conditions.text: Node must have an established peer set providing coverage of the required column subnets.

post_conditions.text: If sampling succeeds, the node considers blob data available for the slot.
If 50%+ columns are obtained, reconstruction SHOULD be triggered.

sub_graphs.name: Reconstruction and Cross-Seeding
sub_graphs.description: Defines the protocol for reconstructing missing columns once a node has at least 50% of all columns, and the cross-seeding behavior to redistribute reconstructed data.

invariants.text: Reconstruction is possible if and only if >= 50% of all columns are available.
Once a column is obtained through reconstruction, the node MUST expose it as if received over the network.
If the node is subscribed to a reconstructed column's subnet, it MUST send the DataColumnSidecar to its mesh neighbors.
If the node is NOT subscribed to the subnet, it SHOULD still expose availability via gossip emission.

pre_conditions.text: Node must have >= 50% of columns for the blob to trigger reconstruction.

post_conditions.text: After reconstruction, the node has a complete matrix view and can serve any column to peers.

title: EIP-7823: Set Upper Bounds for MODEXP
description: Restricts each MODEXP precompile input field to a maximum of 8192 bits (1024 bytes) to reduce consensus bugs and simplify future EVMMAX replacement.

sub_graphs.name: MODEXP Precompile Input Format
sub_graphs.description: Defines the input format for the MODEXP precompile at address 0x05, as inherited from EIP-198.

invariants.text: The MODEXP precompile resides at address 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000005.
Input format is always: <length_of_BASE> <length_of_EXPONENT> <length_of_MODULUS> <BASE> <EXPONENT> <MODULUS>.
Each length field is a 256-bit (32-byte) unsigned integer specifying the byte-length of its corresponding value field.

functions.description: Computes BASE^EXPONENT mod MODULUS. Defined in EIP-198.

data_structures.name: MODEXP Input Layout
data_structures.definition: bytes32(length_of_BASE) ++ bytes32(length_of_EXPONENT) ++ bytes32(length_of_MODULUS) ++ bytes[length_of_BASE](BASE) ++ bytes[length_of_EXPONENT](EXPONENT) ++ bytes[length_of_MODULUS](MODULUS)
data_structures.description: Sequential byte layout of the MODEXP precompile input as defined in EIP-198.

state_variables.description: The address of the MODEXP precompile.

sub_graphs.name: Upper Bound Enforcement on MODEXP Inputs
sub_graphs.description: Introduces a hard upper bound on each of the three length inputs. Each MUST be <= 1024 bytes (8192 bits).

invariants.text: The maximum permitted value for length_of_BASE is 1024 bytes (8192 bits).
The maximum permitted value for length_of_EXPONENT is 1024 bytes (8192 bits).
The maximum permitted value for length_of_MODULUS is 1024 bytes (8192 bits).
The upper bound constant is 1024 bytes = 8192 bits, same for all three fields.
The bound applies to each length field independently; there is no combined/aggregate limit.

post_conditions.text: If all preconditions are met, the precompile proceeds to normal execution (EIP-198 semantics).

functions.signature: validate_modexp_bounds(length_of_BASE: uint256, length_of_EXPONENT: uint256, length_of_MODULUS: uint256) -> bool
functions.description: Validates that all three MODEXP input length fields are within the 1024-byte upper bound.

state_variables.name: MODEXP_INPUT_UPPER_BOUND
state_variables.description: The maximum allowed byte-length for each MODEXP input length field.

sub_graphs.name: MODEXP Error Behavior on Bound Violation
sub_graphs.description: Specifies the error behavior when any MODEXP input length field exceeds the 1024-byte upper bound. The precompile stops execution, returns an error, and consumes ALL provided gas.

invariants.text: When a bound violation occurs, ALL gas provided to the precompile call is consumed.
When a bound violation occurs, the precompile returns an error, producing no output.
The violation of ANY single length field is sufficient to trigger the error path.

pre_conditions.text: At least one length field exceeds 1024 bytes.

post_conditions.text: An error is returned to the caller.
All gas provided to the precompile call is consumed.

state_transitions.from: MODEXP precompile called with oversized input

sub_graphs.name: MODEXP Successful Execution Path
sub_graphs.description: Normal execution path after upper-bound validation passes. Computes modular exponentiation per EIP-198.

invariants.text: The computation semantics (BASE^EXPONENT mod MODULUS) are unchanged from EIP-198.
The gas pricing formula is unchanged from EIP-198.

pre_conditions.text: All three length fields pass the bound validation.

post_conditions.text: The precompile returns BASE^EXPONENT mod MODULUS as a byte array of length equal to length_of_MODULUS.
Gas is consumed according to the EIP-198 pricing formula.

functions.signature: MODEXP_execute(BASE: bytes, EXPONENT: bytes, MODULUS: bytes) -> bytes
functions.description: Executes BASE^EXPONENT mod MODULUS when all length preconditions are satisfied.

state_transitions.name: Valid MODEXP Computation
state_transitions.to: Result returned; gas consumed per EIP-198 pricing
state_transitions.trigger: All length fields pass bound validation

sub_graphs.name: Input Validation Decision Logic
sub_graphs.description: The complete decision tree connecting the bound-check logic to either the error path (SG-003) or the success path (SG-004).

invariants.text: The bound check is performed BEFORE any modular exponentiation computation.
The bound check is performed BEFORE the EIP-198 gas cost calculation.
The three length fields are read from the first 96 bytes of input before the bound check.

sub_graphs.name: Backwards Compatibility Analysis
sub_graphs.description: Empirical analysis confirming the 1024-byte upper bound does not break any historical on-chain usage. Max observed was 513 bytes.

invariants.text: No historical MODEXP call on mainnet (block 5,472,266 through 21,550,926) used a successful input length field exceeding 513 bytes.
The overwhelming majority of historical MODEXP calls use 32-byte input lengths (over 99.7%).
The new 1024-byte limit provides ~2x safety margin over the maximum historically observed value.
This is a backwards-incompatible consensus change, but no past transaction would have behaved differently.

sub_graphs.name: Supported Use Cases Under the Upper Bound
sub_graphs.description: Documents cryptographic use cases that remain fully supported under the 1024-byte (8192-bit) upper bound.

invariants.text: RSA verification with key sizes up to 8192 bits remains fully supported.
Common RSA key sizes (1024, 2048, 4096 bits) are well within the limit.
Elliptic curve use cases (usually < 384 bits) remain fully supported.
The 8192-bit bound provides significant headroom over all known practical use cases.

sub_graphs.name: Security Considerations and Consensus Bug Prevention
sub_graphs.description: Security analysis: the change is purely defensive, reducing the accepted input range from unbounded to a finite, testable domain.

invariants.text: No new security surface area is introduced.
The testing surface for MODEXP is no longer infinite; it is bounded by the 1024-byte limit.
The MODEXP precompile has historically been a source of numerous consensus bugs.
The change strictly reduces the accepted input domain.
